extraction.name: SWE-Gym
extraction.description: An environment for training software engineering (SWE) agents containing 2,438 real-world task instances, each comprising a Python codebase with an executable runtime environment, unit tests, and a task specified in natural language.
extraction.creator: Jiayi Pan, Xingyao Wang, Graham Neubig, Navdeep Jaitly, Heng Ji, Alane Suhr, Yizhe Zhang
extraction.publisher: Proceedings of the 42nd Intemational Conference on Machine Leaming
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Used SEART GitHub search to filter Python repositories created before July 1, 2022, with more than 500 stars, at least 300 lines of code, more than 500 pull requests, and 100 contributors. Used SWE-Bench's instance extraction script to convert these repositories into task instances, and semi-manually created executable environments for them.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Real-world software engineering tasks sourced from pull requests in 11 popular Python repositories (and 358 repositories for SWE-Gym Raw).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Manually configured dependencies for each task instance using relevant configuration files (e.g., requirements.txt), CI scripts, or documentation from the repository snapshot. Used SWE-Bench's execution-based validation script to ensure that the gold patch passes more unit tests than the original code, filtering out failed instances.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Manual configuration of dependencies for each task instance and validation of instances, requiring approximately 200 human annotation hours.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotations are done by a subset of the authors.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: SWE-Bench's instance extraction script, SWE-Bench's execution-based validation script
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Improving automated software engineering capabilities could increase developer productivity and accessibility, but may impact software engineering jobs and require careful consideration around code ownership, licensing, and attribution. Similar techniques could potentially be misused to automate the creation of malicious code.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The task distribution across repositories exhibits a long-tail pattern. Repeated sampling introduces a bias toward easier tasks, which was mitigated using per-instance capping.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limited by its environment diversity, including the number of repositories, types of tasks, and programming languages.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training language model based SWE agents, training verifier models to enable inference-time scaling, and evaluating software engineering performance.
